topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Locality Design
explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to bridge the performance gap between fast, expensive CPU registers and slower, cheaper main memory.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of storage with varying speeds and capacities, each designed to exploit the principle of locality (temporal and spatial). Caching strategies leverage this principle by storing frequently accessed data in faster levels of the hierarchy, reducing the average memory access time.  This is crucial for performance optimization in modern systems.
